value: in high-elevation populations, petal angle fell (petals flattened) by 10° for every 5°C increase in air temperature
method: field petal angle (protractor, 11:00 to 14:00) regressed on flower-level air temperature (thermocouple about 2 cm from each flower), mixed models with elevation as a fixed factor and population nested in elevation as a random effect
conditions: San Juan Mountains, Colorado, 2021; four high-elevation (>3000 m) and five low-elevation (<2600 m) populations; petal angle on 562 flowers (mean 62.4 per population); the next sentence of the text gives the low-elevation response as a reduction of less than 4° per 5°C; the text states that air temperature had little influence on the timing and speed of flower opening and closing (Table S4); model estimates and P values are in supplementary tables that were not read; the paper reports this as behavioural thermoregulation by petal movement and does not measure sun-tracking Air temperature (mean 10:00 to 14:00) was logged only on the 265 probed flowers, so the 562 flowers overstates the sample behind the slope; the field result is an association and irradiance was not measured. The quote is from the main Results text (section 3.2), pointing to Figure S3.

method: cloned genotypes from field populations grown in two Percival chambers, warm (28/15 °C day/night) and cool (14/1 °C), 14 h daylength; petal angle followed over the floral lifespan
conditions: plants from 4 low- and 4 high-elevation populations collected in 2019 and 2020 and kept in the greenhouse; 34 low- and 48 high-elevation genotypes, 147 plants; experiment run in spring 2022 and 2023 with treatments swapped between chambers; on the second day of anthesis high-elevation populations had a steeper petal-angle reaction norm than low, described by the authors as a modest elevation-by-treatment interaction (Figure S4B; Table S7); the same section reports a lower focal point of light in high- than low-elevation flowers in the cold treatment (P = 0.032); estimates for petal angle are in supplementary tables that were not read On day 1 high-elevation flowers were more cupped in both treatments; the text gives no low-elevation lifespan change in petal angle; the direct test of the quoted result is the Table S8 sentence, which is not carried here.
